title: An article's body, every kind of block

blocks.text:
Most pages on a small business site change a few times a year, yet the server builds each one from scratch on every visit. A page cache keeps the finished HTML and hands it straight back, so the *second* visitor never waits for the first one's work.

This piece measures what that saves on an ordinary content site, and where it stops helping.

Without a cache, every request boots the framework, opens a database connection, runs the queries for the page and renders the templates. With one, the request is answered from a file before **any** of that starts.

items.text: Booting the framework and its service providers
Between eight and forty database queries, depending on the page
Rendering the layout, the sections and the *partials* inside them

A cache hides a slow page; it doesn't make it fast. Pages behind a login, a basket or a search still run the full request, so they're worth measuring on their own.

html:
Most pages on a small business site change a few times a year, yet the server builds each one from scratch on every visit. A page cache keeps the finished HTML and hands it straight back, so the second visitor never waits for the first one's work.

This piece measures what that saves on an ordinary content site, and where it stops helping.

01 What a page cache actually skips

Without a cache, every request boots the framework, opens a database connection, runs the queries for the page and renders the templates. With one, the request is answered from a file before any of that starts.

  • Booting the framework and its service providers
  • Between eight and forty database queries, depending on the page
  • Rendering the layout, the sections and the partials inside them
to render the page cold
28 ms
to serve the same page from disk
4.4 ms

02 How it was measured

Each page was requested 500 times from the same machine, after a warm-up of 50, with the median taken. The check runs before the session starts, so a cached page costs one file read.

Median response time, 500 requests per page
Page Cold Cached
Home 31 ms 4.6 ms
Service page 28 ms 4.4 ms
Article 36 ms 4.5 ms

03 When to clear it

  1. Clear a page when it's saved in the editor.
  2. Clear every page when the menu or the footer changes.
  3. Never cache a page with a form's error messages on it.

What it doesn't fix

A cache hides a slow page; it doesn't make it fast. Pages behind a login, a basket or a search still run the full request, so they're worth measuring on their own.

A short, straight answer: two or three sentences, with the detail people actually need before they get in touch.

No. Quotes are free and in writing, usually within a day.

Leeds and anywhere within about 20 miles.
